citations.quote: The efficacy results from HELIOS-A (Study 002) support the approval of vutrisiran for the treatment of polyneuropathy in adult patients with hATTR amyloidosis.

During the review, it was determined that vutrisiran was initially supplied for the HELIOS-A study (ALN-TTRSC02-002) in a vial and later in a pre-filled syringe, and that subjects received various combinations of vial and syringe administrations.
The efficacy of AMVUTTRA was evaluated in a randomized, open-label clinical trial in adult patients with polyneuropathy caused by hATTR amyloidosis (Study 1; NCT03759379).
HELIOS-A is an ongoing, 18-month, Phase 3, randomized, open-label, externally-controlled study of vutrisiran using the placebo treatment arm from the APOLLO study as a comparator.

design.text: 18-month, randomized, open-label, externally-controlled study using the placebo arm from the APOLLO study as comparator and patisiran as an active control; randomized 3:1 to vutrisiran or patisiran.

citations.quote: HELIOS-A is an ongoing, 18-month, Phase 3, randomized, open-label, externally-controlled study of vutrisiran using the placebo treatment arm from the APOLLO study as a comparator.
In HELIOS-A, a total of 164 subjects were randomized 3:1 to receive either vutrisiran 25 mg SC every three months (Q3M), or patisiran 0.3mg/kg IV once every three weeks (Q3W).

population.text: Adult patients (18 to 85 years) with hATTR amyloidosis with a documented TTR gene mutation and baseline NIS of 5 to 130.

citations.quote: Subjects were required to be between 18 and 85 years of age (inclusive) and have a diagnosis of hATTR amyloidosis with a documented mutation in the TTR gene. Subjects were also required to have a baseline NIS of 5 to 130 where higher scores indicate more severe polyneuropathy.

endpoint.text: Change from baseline to Month 9 in the modified neuropathy impairment score +7 (mNIS+7) compared to the APOLLO placebo group.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the change from baseline to Month 9 in the modified neuropathy impairment score +7 (mNIS+7) as compared to the placebo group from the APOLLO study at Month 9, analyzed using general ANCOVA/multiple imputation methods of the mITT population.

n.text: 164 randomized in HELIOS-A (122 vutrisiran, 42 patisiran); 77 external placebo subjects from APOLLO.

citations.quote: HELIOS-A enrolled 164 subjects (122 vutrisiran-treated, and 42 patisiran-treated). There were 77 placebo-treated subjects from APOLLO for the external comparator group.

result.text: At Month 9, mNIS+7 change from baseline was -2.2 for vutrisiran vs 14.8 for placebo; LS mean difference -17.0 (95% CI -21.8, -12.2), p<0.0001. Norfolk QoL-DN LS mean difference -16.2 (95% CI -21.7, -10.8), p<0.0001.

target_moa.text: Vutrisiran is a transthyretin-directed double-stranded siRNA-GalNAc conjugate that degrades mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA via RNA interference, reducing serum TTR protein and TTR deposits in tissues.

citations.quote: Vutrisiran is a double-stranded siRNA-GalNAc conjugate that causes degradation of mutant and wild-type TTR mRNA through RNA interference, which results in a reduction of serum TTR protein and TTR protein deposits in tissues.

summary.text: NDA 215515 for vutrisiran was submitted by Alnylam and received April 14, 2021 with a PDUFA goal date of July 14, 2022. Vutrisiran had Orphan Drug designation (5/25/2018) and Fast Track designation (4/3/2020), was approved on a traditional (not accelerated) basis on one adequate and well-controlled trial (HELIOS-A) plus confirmatory evidence, and was not referred to an advisory committee.

Applicant	Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
Date of Submission	April 14, 2021
PDUFA Goal Date	July 14, 2022
On May 25, 2018, vutrisiran was granted an Orphan Drug designation and received a Fast-Track designation on April 3, 2020. Vutrisiran is not approved in any other jurisdiction.
The application meets the substantial evidence standard based on one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation plus confirmatory evidence.
This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the application did not raise significant efficacy or safety issues in the intended population.
